label: 2.0.32 SessionDomain is a closed 16-method Pick with no message-read method, and the 2.0.32 plugin Context lists 27 domains with no client key, so both gate plugins' defensive ctx.client.session.messages calls short-circuit to null on v2: the spec gate stays permanently open (allow) and the completion sentinel permanently silent, with no thrown error or log to observe. Any version-aware port must convert these guards into positive capability assertions because the existing defensive guards are exactly what hides the break.

The real 2.0.32 execute.after payload is {tool:string, sessionID, agent, messageID, id:Tool.CallID, input:unknown} intersected with a status-tagged union {status:'completed', result:Tool.Result} | {status:'error', error:Tool.Error}: the tool result body is exposed under result, discriminated by status, and input is unknown so it needs per-tool narrowing. It is registered on ctx.tool.hook('execute.after') because SessionHooks contains no execute.after, correcting iteration 3's ctx.session.hook('execute.after') phrasing.

The 2.0.32 session context hook event is SessionContext, extending SessionRequest with sessionID, model:Model.Ref, a deliberately non-readonly system:SystemPart[], messages:Message[], options:SessionRequestOptions, plus agent:Agent.ID and tools:Record<string,{description,input:JsonSchema}>. Because system is mutable a plugin rewrites the system prompt in place instead of re-prompting, and because SessionContext is the only structure carrying messages it is simultaneously the message-read substitute and skill-advisor's injection point.

v2 has no compaction-completed event; it has a compaction interception hook (SessionCompaction extends SessionContext with result?:SessionCompactionResult, documented as skipping the model request when set) plus a session.compact RPC. So skill-advisor's post-compaction re-injection becomes a pre-request system mutation rather than an event re-arm, while spec-gate's re-arm has no peer at all. There is also no idle event in the contract; the only push candidate remains iteration 4's unconfirmed session.execution.succeeded|failed|interrupted derivation, with session.wait as the sole pull primitive.

The 2.0.32 OpenAPI publishes no event-type vocabulary: /api/event (operationId event.subscribe) returns text/event-stream with envelope {id:string|null, event:string, data:V2EventEncoded} and V2EventEncoded resolves to a bare {type:'string', contentMediaType:'application/json'}. A grep across 36 event-ish namespace prefixes found only plugin-RPC method identifiers and no native event names among 293 schemas, so the v1 permission.asked/question.*/message.part.updated to v2 map is not derivable from the contract. The same operation states the stream is volatile by contract with guaranteed missed events during disconnection, which forbids treating any event as a ledger entry and requires idempotent, reconcilable consumers.

2.0.32 declares Plugin as {readonly id:string, readonly setup:(context)=>Promise<Cleanup|void>|Cleanup|void} and define(plugin:Plugin):Plugin with no runtime validator in the .d.ts, so keys beyond id/setup are rejected only by TypeScript's excess-property check and runtime tolerance stays UNVERIFIED. The 2.0.32 Context has no client, tui, ui, data, attention or renderer key, closing ctx.tui as a dead end and confirming iteration 4's conclusion from the opposite direction: toast rendering is reachable only via the separate ./tui export, never from a server plugin. EventDomain is only Pick<EventApi,'subscribe'>.

Seven 2.0.32 context domains have no v1 peer and must be reached only behind a presence branch: plugin (Pick<PluginApi,'list'>), rpc, storage, worktree, vcs, reference, generate, plus experimental.terminal (Pick of the persistentPty read). This is the mirror image of the v1-only client, so a shared dual-target module needs capability branching in both directions rather than a single feature probe.

Scope-limited: the __test plugin-definition probe and the opencode2 api GET /api/plugin call were not executed because both need a probe directory outside the allowed-write list. plugin.check in the contract is the sanctioned settlement route.
